name: Chip supply
value: US licence rule for 5 chip-diversion states
summary: US required licences from 16 Nov for advanced AI chips to five countries to curb diversion to China; no TSMC stoppage
state: On 16 Nov the US Commerce Department required export licences for advanced AI chips shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, aiming to stop Chinese firms reaching them through overseas data centres (Al Jazeera, 17 Nov; SCMP). Searches on 20 Nov found no TSMC or Samsung output disruption, so new controls keep Watch.
for_you: Tighter controls tend to lengthen lead times for servers and AI hardware rather than cause shortages in shops.
rubric_hit: Watch: new US export controls on advanced AI chips from 16 Nov; no major TSMC/Samsung output disruption found

sources.title: Al Jazeera — US moves to block China's remote access to AI chips amid Nvidia scandal
South China Morning Post — US tightens AI chip export curbs to close China's overseas data centre loophole

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
